---
title: "Model Selection and Regularization"
---

This lecture asks how to improve linear models when there are many
candidate predictors, correlated variables, or a need for sparse and
stable predictions.

## Learning Objectives

- Compare best subset, forward stepwise, and backward stepwise
  selection.
- Explain ridge regression and lasso as constrained optimization
  problems.
- Interpret the role of the tuning parameter.
- Use cross-validation to choose model complexity.

## Core Ideas

Subset selection searches over models. Regularization changes the
objective so that large or numerous coefficients are penalized:

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i - x_i^\top \beta)^2 + \lambda P(\beta).
$$

Different penalties encode different preferences about complexity.

## Worked Example

Use a regression data set with several predictors to compare stepwise
selection, ridge, and lasso under cross-validation.

## Selection Workflow

Classical model selection provides a useful baseline before
regularization. Start by comparing forward selection, backward
elimination, and best subset selection.

```r
null_model <- lm(SalePrice ~ 1, data = train)
full_model <- lm(SalePrice ~ ., data = train)

forward_model <- step(
  null_model,
  scope = list(lower = null_model, upper = full_model),
  direction = "forward"
)

backward_model <- step(full_model, direction = "backward")
```

This gives students a concrete path from "all possible predictors" to a
selected linear model. The important caution is that stepwise procedures
can overstate certainty because the same data are used to search and
estimate.

## Comparing Selection Criteria

Compare candidate models using AIC, BIC, adjusted $R^2$, prediction
error, and visual predicted-versus-actual checks:

| Criterion | What it rewards | Caution |
|---|---|---|
| Adjusted $R^2$ | In-sample fit with a complexity adjustment | Still tied to the training sample. |
| AIC | Predictive fit with a lighter penalty | Can choose larger models. |
| BIC | Fit with a stronger complexity penalty | Can prefer simpler models. |
| Cross-validation error | Estimated out-of-sample performance | Depends on the resampling design. |
| Test error | Final held-out performance | Use once, after model selection. |

This section should prepare students for ridge and lasso by showing the
limits of discrete model search.

## Applied Practice

Practice by comparing best subset selection, forward selection, and
backward selection on the same regression task. Then fit ridge and
lasso models with cross-validation. Report the selected predictors,
test-set error, and the tradeoff between accuracy, stability, and
interpretability.
